name.en: Ancestral Polynesian society in Tonga and Samoa
name.zh: 汤加与萨摩亚的祖先波利尼西亚社会

summary.en: Descendants of the Lapita voyagers, who had reached Tonga and Samoa by about 850 BCE, developed a distinctive Polynesian language, religion and way of life during a long pause of more than a millennium before anyone sailed further east. Pottery-making faded out early in the first millennium CE.
summary.zh: 拉皮塔航海者约在公元前850年已抵达汤加和萨摩亚，其后裔在此后一千多年的“漫长停顿”中，形成了独特的波利尼西亚语言、宗教和生活方式，之后才有人继续东航。公元1千纪初，制陶传统逐渐消失。

sources.title: P. V. Kirch & R. C. Green, Hawaiki, Ancestral Polynesia: An Essay in Historical Anthropology (Cambridge University Press, 2001)
Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Pacific migrations
UNESCO: Lapita pottery and the peopling of Remote Oceania (Pacific heritage hub)

note: An ancient continuity, not a dated event: the range marks the atlas span up to the start of East Polynesian voyaging. Lapita itself (c. 1350–500 BCE) is older than the atlas.

story.en:
About 3,000 years ago people making finely stamped Lapita pottery sailed out of the Bismarck Archipelago and, within a few centuries, crossed more than 3,000 km of open sea to Vanuatu, New Caledonia, Fiji, Tonga and Samoa. They carried pigs, dogs, chickens, taro, yams and breadfruit, and their Austronesian language was the ancestor of every Polynesian tongue.

In Tonga and Samoa the voyaging then stopped for well over a thousand years. Archaeologists call it the long pause. In those centuries the islanders' pottery became plain and then disappeared, and linguists reconstruct a shared Proto-Polynesian vocabulary for chiefs (ariki), sacred restriction (tapu), spiritual power (mana) and the ceremonial ground (malaʻe, later marae).

This was Hawaiki, the homeland that later Polynesians remembered in their genealogies. When voyagers finally pushed east after about 900 CE, they took with them the institutions formed during the pause, which is why Hawaiians, Tahitians, Māori and Rapa Nui share so much.
story.zh:
大约3000年前，制作精美压印纹拉皮塔陶器的人群驶出俾斯麦群岛，在数百年内跨越三千多公里的开阔海域，抵达瓦努阿图、新喀里多尼亚、斐济、汤加和萨摩亚。他们带着猪、狗、鸡、芋头、薯蓣和面包果，其南岛语是所有波利尼西亚语言的祖先。

此后，汤加和萨摩亚的航海活动停顿了一千多年，考古学家称之为“漫长停顿”。在这几个世纪里，岛民的陶器先是变得素面无纹，继而完全消失；语言学家据此重建出共同的原始波利尼西亚语词汇，如酋长（ariki）、禁忌（tapu）、神力（mana）和仪式场地（malaʻe，后来的marae）。

这就是后来波利尼西亚人在谱系中追忆的故乡“哈瓦基”。约900年后航海者终于继续东进时，他们带走了在停顿期形成的制度，这正是夏威夷人、塔希提人、毛利人和拉帕努伊人有如此多共同之处的原因。

name.zh: 陶波火山哈特佩喷发

summary.en: The Taupō volcano in the North Island of New Zealand erupted around 232 CE in one of the most violent eruptions of the last 5,000 years, devastating some 20,000 km² with pyroclastic flows and enlarging Lake Taupō. The land was still uninhabited by people.
summary.zh: 约公元232年，新西兰北岛陶波火山爆发，是近5000年来最猛烈的火山喷发之一，火山碎屑流摧毁了约两万平方公里的土地，并扩大了陶波湖。当时这片土地尚无人类居住。

sources.title: A. Hogg et al., 'Revised calendar date for the Taupo eruption derived by 14C wiggle-matching', The Holocene 22 (2012)
GNS Science: Taupō Volcanic Centre
Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Historic volcanic activity – Taupō

note: Wiggle-matched radiocarbon dates give 232 ± 10 CE; older literature cites 186 CE.

name.zh: 波利尼西亚航海者定居东波利尼西亚

summary.en: In one of humanity's greatest feats of exploration, Polynesian navigators in double-hulled canoes, steering by stars, swells and birds, settled the Society Islands around 1000, then Hawaiʻi, the Marquesas, Rapa Nui and finally Aotearoa New Zealand by about 1300, spanning an ocean triangle of some 30 million km².
summary.zh: 这是人类最伟大的探索壮举之一：波利尼西亚航海者驾驶双体独木舟，凭星辰、涌浪和海鸟导航，约在1000年定居社会群岛，随后是夏威夷、马克萨斯、拉帕努伊，约1300年最终抵达新西兰奥特亚罗瓦，覆盖约三千万平方公里的海洋三角区。

sources.title: J. M. Wilmshurst et al., 'High-precision radiocarbon dating shows recent and rapid initial human colonization of East Polynesia', PNAS 108 (2011)
P. V. Kirch, On the Road of the Winds: An Archaeological History of the Pacific Islands (University of California Press, 2nd ed. 2017)
Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Pacific migrations

note: Dates follow the 'short chronology' of Wilmshurst et al. (2011); some archaeologists argue Hawaiʻi and the Marquesas were reached a century or two earlier. Route years are approximate.

story.en:
After the long pause in Tonga and Samoa, voyagers began to sail east around the turn of the first millennium. Radiocarbon dates from short-lived plant remains suggest the Society Islands were reached around 1025–1120, and that within a few generations people had spread to almost every habitable island of the eastern Pacific, a burst of exploration over thousands of kilometres of open ocean.

They sailed double-hulled canoes that could carry dozens of people with plants and animals. Navigators read the rising and setting points of stars, the feel of ocean swells against the hull, the flight of land-based birds and the colour of clouds over unseen islands. Many voyages sailed into the prevailing easterly winds, a sensible strategy: a canoe that found nothing could run home downwind.

The last great landfalls were Rapa Nui and, around 1250–1300, Aotearoa. By then a network of two-way voyaging linked the Societies, the Cooks, the Australs and Mangareva. Later, around 1450, much long-distance voyaging ceased, and islands like Hawaiʻi and New Zealand developed on their own.
story.zh:
在汤加和萨摩亚漫长停顿之后，约在第一个千年之交，航海者开始向东航行。短寿植物遗存的放射性碳测年表明，社会群岛约在1025至1120年间被抵达，此后短短几代人之内，人们便扩散到东太平洋几乎所有宜居岛屿，这是一场跨越数千公里开阔海洋的探索浪潮。

他们驾驶的双体独木舟能载数十人以及植物和牲畜。航海师观察星辰的升落方位、船体感受到的涌浪、陆栖海鸟的飞行方向，以及看不见的岛屿上空云彩的颜色。许多航程逆着盛行东风而行，这是明智的策略：若一无所获，独木舟可以顺风返航。

最后的重大登陆是拉帕努伊，以及约1250至1300年的奥特亚罗瓦。那时，社会群岛、库克群岛、南方群岛和芒阿雷瓦之间已形成往返航行的网络。约1450年后，远程航行大多停止，夏威夷和新西兰等岛屿开始各自独立发展。

name.en: Taputapuātea, sacred centre of East Polynesia
name.zh: 塔普塔普阿特阿：东波利尼西亚的神圣中心

summary.en: At Opoa on Raʻiatea, the marae complex of Taputapuātea became the religious heart of the Society Islands and a gathering place for voyagers from across East Polynesia; stones from it were carried to found new marae elsewhere. It was the centre of the cult of ʻOro and is a UNESCO World Heritage site (2017).
summary.zh: 赖阿特阿岛奥波阿的塔普塔普阿特阿马拉埃建筑群成为社会群岛的宗教中心，也是东波利尼西亚各地航海者的聚会地；人们从这里取石到别处建立新的马拉埃。这里是奥罗神崇拜的中心，2017年列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Taputapuātea
P. V. Kirch, On the Road of the Winds (2nd ed. 2017)

note: The site's sacred role is placed near the settlement of the Society Islands; the surviving stone ahu were largely built or rebuilt from about the 17th century.

name.zh: 波利尼西亚人与美洲原住民相遇

summary.en: Genome studies of modern Polynesians show that people from the eastern Pacific mixed with a Native American group related to Colombia's Zenú around 1150–1230, first in the southern Marquesas. The South American sweet potato, kūmara, had already spread through East Polynesia, the clearest proof of pre-Columbian contact.
summary.zh: 对现代波利尼西亚人的基因组研究表明，约1150至1230年间，东太平洋居民与一支与哥伦比亚泽努人相关的美洲原住民群体发生混血，最早见于马克萨斯群岛南部。原产南美的甘薯（kūmara）早已传遍东波利尼西亚，这是前哥伦布时代接触最明确的证据。

sources.title: A. G. Ioannidis et al., 'Native American gene flow into Polynesia predating Easter Island settlement', Nature 583 (2020)
C. Roullier et al., 'Historical collections reveal patterns of diffusion of sweet potato in Oceania', PNAS 110 (2013)

note: Whether Polynesians reached America or Americans drifted into Polynesia is unresolved; most scholars favour Polynesian voyages.

name.zh: 巨石城南马都尔的建造

summary.en: Off the east coast of Pohnpei the Saudeleur rulers raised nearly a hundred artificial islets of stacked basalt columns and coral fill, linked by canals. Its megalithic phase began around 1180–1200; it held royal residences, priests' quarters and the walled mortuary islet of Nandauwas. UNESCO listed it in 2016.
summary.zh: 在波纳佩岛东岸外，绍德雷尔统治者用层层叠架的玄武岩石柱和珊瑚碎石筑起近百座人工岛，以水道相连。其巨石建筑阶段约始于1180至1200年，岛上有王室居所、祭司区和围墙环绕的南道瓦斯墓葬岛。2016年列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Nan Madol: Ceremonial Centre of Eastern Micronesia
M. D. McCoy et al., 'Earliest direct evidence of monument building at the archaeological site of Nan Madol (Pohnpei, Micronesia) identified using 230Th/U coral dating', Quaternary Research 86 (2016)
Smithsonian Magazine: Nan Madol, the city built on coral reefs

note: Coral dating places the first monumental building at about 1180–1200; the Saudeleur era ended c. 1628.

story.en:
Nan Madol covers about 80 hectares of reef flat. Its builders quarried columnar basalt on the far side of Pohnpei, prisms up to six metres long and weighing several tonnes each, and stacked them header-and-stretcher fashion like a log cabin to make walls up to seven metres high. How they moved roughly 750,000 tonnes of stone remains debated; rafts and canals are the usual explanation, flying sorcery the traditional one.

The city was divided in two. Madol Powe, the upper town, was for priests and the dead; its greatest enclosure, Nandauwas, held the tombs of the Saudeleur lords. Madol Pah, the lower town, held administrative and residential islets. Food for the court came as tribute from the whole island, and turtles were kept for ceremonial feasts.

In 2016 dating of coral used as construction fill showed that monument building had begun by about 1180, making Nan Madol the earliest known centre of megalithic royal power in the Pacific islands. Today rising seas and mangroves threaten the site, which is on UNESCO's danger list.
story.zh:
南马都尔占地约80公顷的礁坪。建造者在波纳佩岛另一侧开采柱状玄武岩，单根长达六米、重达数吨，以纵横交错的方式像搭木屋一样堆叠，筑成高达七米的墙体。他们如何搬运约75万吨石料至今仍有争论：通常的解释是木筏和水道，传统的说法则是巫师的飞行法术。

城市分为两部分。上城马多尔·波韦供祭司和亡者使用，其中最大的围院南道瓦斯安葬着绍德雷尔诸王。下城马多尔·帕赫则有行政和居住岛屿。宫廷所需食物由全岛作为贡赋供应，海龟被饲养以供仪式宴会。

2016年，对用作填料的珊瑚进行测年表明，巨石建造约始于1180年，使南马都尔成为太平洋岛屿已知最早的巨石王权中心。如今海平面上升和红树林正威胁着遗址，它已被列入联合国教科文组织濒危遗产名录。

name.zh: 哈阿蒙加毛伊三石门

summary.en: A trilithon of three coral-limestone slabs, each weighing some 30–40 tonnes, raised on Tongatapu around 1200 and attributed by tradition to the eleventh Tuʻi Tonga, Tuʻitātui. Its name means 'Maui's burden'; Tāufaʻāhau Tupou IV argued in 1967 that notches on the lintel marked the solstices.
summary.zh: 汤加塔布岛上由三块珊瑚石灰岩巨石组成的三石门，每块重约30至40吨，约建于1200年，传统认为出自第十一代图伊汤加图伊塔图伊之手。其名意为“毛伊的担子”；1967年陶法阿豪·图普四世提出，横梁上的刻痕标示着冬至与夏至。

sources.title: Tonga Ministry of Tourism: Haʻamonga ʻa Maui
G. Clark, D. Burley & T. Murray, 'Monumentality and the development of the Tongan maritime chiefdom', Antiquity 82 (2008)

note: Date and builder come from royal genealogies; the solstice interpretation is a modern hypothesis.

name.zh: 拉帕努伊人雕刻摩艾石像

summary.en: The people of Rapa Nui carved nearly a thousand monolithic moai from the tuff of the Rano Raraku crater and set many on stone platforms (ahu) facing inland over their kin groups, as embodiments of deified ancestors. Carving peaked between about 1300 and 1600.
summary.zh: 拉帕努伊岛民从拉诺拉拉库火山口的凝灰岩中凿出近千尊巨石摩艾像，并把其中许多立在石台（阿胡）上，面朝内陆守护各自的亲族群体，作为神化祖先的化身。雕刻活动在约1300至1600年间达到高峰。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Rapa Nui National Park
T. L. Hunt & C. P. Lipo, The Statues That Walked (Free Press, 2011)
R. J. DiNapoli et al., 'A model-based approach to the tempo of monument construction on Rapa Nui', Nature Communications 11 (2020)

note: Construction chronologies are debated; DiNapoli et al. (2020) show ahu building began soon after settlement and continued after European contact in 1722.

story.en:
Rapa Nui is one of the most isolated inhabited places on earth, about 2,000 km from Pitcairn and 3,700 km from Chile. The Polynesians who settled it around 1200 organised themselves into kin groups, each of which built ahu platforms along the coast and raised moai on them, eyes of white coral and red scoria topknots (pukao) in place.

Almost all moai came from one quarry, Rano Raraku, where about 400 still lie unfinished or standing on the slopes. Islanders' traditions say the statues walked to their ahu, and experiments in 2012 showed that a team rocking an upright moai with ropes can 'walk' it forward, matching the road-side statues that fell along ancient routes.

A popular story holds that the islanders destroyed their own forests and society. Recent research tells a more complicated story: rats introduced by the first settlers ate palm seeds, people farmed intensively with rock gardens, and monument building continued after Roggeveen arrived in 1722. The catastrophe came later, with smallpox and the Peruvian slave raids of 1862–63.
story.zh:
拉帕努伊是地球上最偏远的有人居住地之一，距皮特凯恩岛约2000公里，距智利约3700公里。约1200年定居于此的波利尼西亚人以亲族群体为单位，各自沿海岸修建阿胡石台，并在上面竖起摩艾像，镶嵌白珊瑚眼睛，戴上红色火山渣制成的发髻（普考）。

几乎所有摩艾都出自同一采石场拉诺拉拉库，那里至今仍有约400尊未完工或立在山坡上的石像。岛民传说石像是自己“走”到阿胡上去的；2012年的实验表明，一组人用绳索左右摇动直立的摩艾，确实可以让它“走”向前方，这与古道旁倒伏的石像相吻合。

流行的说法认为岛民毁掉了自己的森林和社会。近年研究则揭示了更复杂的图景：最早的定居者带来的老鼠啃食棕榈种子，人们用石块园圃精耕细作，而且1722年罗赫芬到来之后石台建造仍在继续。真正的灾难来得更晚，是天花以及1862至1863年秘鲁奴隶贩子的掳掠。

name.zh: 波利尼西亚人定居奥特亚罗瓦

summary.en: Voyagers from East Polynesia, remembered in Māori tradition through canoes such as Tainui, Te Arawa, Mataatua and Tākitimu, settled New Zealand around 1250–1300, the last large landmass on earth to be peopled. Early sites like Wairau Bar show them hunting moa and seals and trading obsidian.
summary.zh: 来自东波利尼西亚的航海者约在1250至1300年定居新西兰，毛利传统通过泰努伊、特阿拉瓦、马塔阿图阿、塔基蒂穆等独木舟铭记这段历史。新西兰是地球上最后有人定居的大块陆地。怀劳沙洲等早期遗址显示他们猎捕恐鸟和海豹，并交易黑曜石。

sources.title: Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Polynesian migrations to New Zealand
J. M. Wilmshurst et al., 'Dating the late prehistoric dispersal of Polynesians to New Zealand using the commensal Pacific rat', PNAS 105 (2008)
NZHistory: Māori arrival and settlement

note: Most archaeologists accept c. 1250–1300; the idea of a single 'Great Fleet' in 1350 was a 20th-century construction by S. Percy Smith and is not supported by tradition or evidence.

story.en:
Māori traditions tell of Kupe, who chased a giant octopus across the ocean from Hawaiki and found a land beneath a long cloud. Later, each iwi traces its ancestors to particular waka, canoes such as Tainui, which landed at Kāwhia, and Te Arawa, which reached Maketū. These genealogies, recited over generations, place the arrivals roughly twenty to thirty generations before the present.

Science agrees remarkably well. The bones of the Pacific rat, which came only with people, and seeds gnawed by it date no earlier than about 1280. At Wairau Bar in Marlborough, one of the earliest villages, archaeologists found moa-egg water bottles, adzes of Marquesan and Society Islands style, and burials whose isotopes suggest some people grew up elsewhere.

The newcomers found an island continent without mammals other than bats. Within a few generations they had hunted the moa to extinction and adapted their tropical crops, especially kūmara, to a cold climate. The idea of a single Great Fleet in 1350 was a misreading by a 20th-century ethnographer.
story.zh:
毛利传统讲述了库佩的故事：他从哈瓦基一路追逐一只巨型章鱼渡海，发现了一片笼罩在长云之下的土地。后来，各部落都把祖先追溯到某艘特定的独木舟，例如在卡菲亚登陆的泰努伊号、抵达马凯图的特阿拉瓦号。这些世代口传的谱系把到达时间定在约二三十代人之前。

科学证据与之惊人地吻合。只会随人类而来的太平洋鼠，其骨骼和啃过的种子年代都不早于约1280年。在马尔堡的怀劳沙洲这一最早的村落之一，考古学家发现了用恐鸟蛋做的水壶、具有马克萨斯和社会群岛风格的石锛，以及同位素显示部分墓主在别处长大的墓葬。

新来者发现的是一片除蝙蝠外没有哺乳动物的岛屿大陆。几代人之内，他们就把恐鸟猎杀殆尽，并把热带作物尤其是甘薯改良为适应寒冷气候的品种。所谓1350年“大船队”的说法，实为20世纪一位民族学家的误读。

name.zh: 科斯雷王城莱卢

summary.en: On a small island off Kosrae, Micronesia, paramount chiefs built Leluh, a walled city of basalt-and-coral compounds, canals and royal tombs that housed perhaps 1,500 people at its height around 1400–1800. Kosraean tradition links it with Isokelekel, conqueror of Nan Madol.
summary.zh: 在密克罗尼西亚科斯雷岛外的一座小岛上，最高酋长们修建了莱卢城，城内有玄武岩与珊瑚砌成的院落、水道和王陵，全盛时期（约1400–1800年）或有1500人居住。科斯雷传统把它与征服南马都尔的伊索克雷克尔联系在一起。

sources.title: R. Cordy, The Lelu Stone Ruins (Kosrae, Micronesia): 1978–81 Historical and Archaeological Research (University of Hawaii, 1993)
Wikipedia: Leluh

note: Construction began perhaps c. 1250 and the city was largely abandoned in the 19th century after epidemics; dates are approximate.

name.zh: 恐鸟灭绝

summary.en: All nine species of moa, giant flightless birds up to 3.6 m tall, were hunted to extinction within about 150–200 years of human arrival in New Zealand, by around 1400. Their predator, Haast's eagle, vanished with them. It is one of the fastest megafaunal extinctions on record.
summary.zh: 九种恐鸟是身高可达3.6米的巨型不飞鸟类，在人类抵达新西兰后约150至200年内，即约1400年前后被猎杀殆尽。以它们为食的哈斯特鹰也随之消失。这是有记录以来最快的大型动物灭绝之一。

sources.title: M. E. Allentoft et al., 'Extinct New Zealand megafauna were not in decline before human colonization', PNAS 111 (2014)
Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Moa

note: Estimates for the final extinction range from c. 1400 to the mid-1400s.

name.en: Moriori and Nunuku's law on Rēkohu
name.zh: 雷科胡岛上的莫里奥里人与努努库之法

summary.en: Polynesians who settled the Chatham Islands (Rēkohu) from mainland New Zealand around 1500 developed a distinct Moriori culture. Tradition says the chief Nunuku-whenua forbade killing in war, a covenant they kept when Ngāti Mutunga and Ngāti Tama invaded in 1835 and killed or enslaved most of them.
summary.zh: 约1500年，从新西兰本土迁居查塔姆群岛（雷科胡）的波利尼西亚人发展出独特的莫里奥里文化。传说酋长努努库-费努阿禁止在战争中杀人，1835年恩加蒂穆通加和恩加蒂塔马部落入侵时他们仍坚守这一誓约，结果多数人被杀或沦为奴隶。

sources.title: Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: Moriori
M. King, Moriori: A People Rediscovered (Viking, 1989)
Moriori Claims Settlement Act 2021 (New Zealand)

note: Settlement date is approximate (c. 1500); the 19th-century myth of Moriori as pre-Māori Melanesians is false.

story.en:
The Chatham Islands lie 800 km east of New Zealand, cold and windswept, without the warmth to grow kūmara. The Polynesians who settled there around 1500 became Moriori, living on seals, birds, fish and fern root, and carving figures into the bark of living kōpī trees (dendroglyphs).

According to Moriori tradition, after a period of bloodshed the ancestor Nunuku-whenua laid down a law: fighting could continue only with sticks the thickness of a thumb, and must stop at first blood. Nunuku's law kept peace on Rēkohu for generations.

In late 1835 about 900 Ngāti Mutunga and Ngāti Tama, displaced by the Musket Wars, arrived on a chartered European brig. Moriori elders met at Te Awapātiki and decided to keep their covenant rather than fight. Some 300 were killed and the rest enslaved; by 1862 only 101 survived. Colonial writers later spread the myth that the Moriori had been a separate, inferior race. In 2020 the Crown apologised and in 2021 passed a settlement act recognising them.
story.zh:
查塔姆群岛位于新西兰以东800公里，寒冷多风，气候不足以种植甘薯。约1500年在此定居的波利尼西亚人成为莫里奥里人，以海豹、鸟类、鱼和蕨根为食，并在活的科皮树树皮上刻画人像（树雕）。

据莫里奥里传统，经历一段流血时期后，祖先努努库-费努阿立下法规：争斗只能用拇指粗细的棍棒，见血即止。“努努库之法”使雷科胡和平延续了许多世代。

1835年底，约900名因火枪战争流离失所的恩加蒂穆通加和恩加蒂塔马族人搭乘一艘租来的欧洲双桅船登岛。莫里奥里长老在特阿瓦帕蒂基集会，决定坚守誓约而不抵抗。约300人被杀，其余沦为奴隶；到1862年仅存101人。殖民作家后来散布莫里奥里人是另一个“劣等”种族的谬说。2020年王室正式道歉，2021年通过和解法案承认其权利。

name.zh: 麦哲伦船队抵达关岛

summary.en: After 99 days crossing the Pacific, Magellan's starving crews made landfall at Guam, the first recorded European contact with Micronesia. When Chamorro islanders took a skiff, Magellan burned houses and killed several people, naming the archipelago the 'Islands of Thieves'. The full voyage is the Magellan–Elcano circumnavigation.
summary.zh: 横渡太平洋99天后，麦哲伦饥肠辘辘的船员在关岛登陆，这是欧洲人与密克罗尼西亚有记录的首次接触。查莫罗岛民取走一艘小艇后，麦哲伦焚烧房屋、杀死数人，并把群岛称为“盗贼群岛”。整个航程见“麦哲伦—埃尔卡诺环球航行”。

sources.title: A. Pigafetta, Relazione del primo viaggio intorno al mondo (c. 1524)
Guampedia: Magellan's landfall in the Marianas
Britannica: Ferdinand Magellan

note: Umatac is the traditional landing place; some historians argue for Rota or another bay on Guam. Linked to ev-magellan-elcano-circumnavigation (europe dataset).

story.en:
Magellan's three surviving ships entered the Pacific in late November 1520 and saw almost no land for more than three months. Antonio Pigafetta recorded that the crew ate biscuit crawling with worms, ox-hide softened in seawater, sawdust and rats, and that nineteen men died of scurvy.

On 6 March 1521 they sighted Guam. Chamorro outrigger canoes came out at once, sailing so fast around the ships that the Europeans were astonished. Islanders boarded and took small items, then the skiff of the flagship; in the Chamorro world of exchange, visitors' goods were not private property in the European sense. Magellan landed armed men, burned forty or fifty houses and killed seven people, then traded for fresh food and left after three days.

The name Islas de los Ladrones, Islands of Thieves, stuck for centuries. Magellan sailed on to the Philippines, where he was killed at Mactan seven weeks later.
story.zh:
1520年11月下旬，麦哲伦剩下的三艘船进入太平洋，此后三个多月几乎不见陆地。安东尼奥·皮加费塔记录道，船员吃的是生满蛆虫的饼干、在海水里泡软的牛皮、木屑和老鼠，有十九人死于坏血病。

1521年3月6日，他们望见关岛。查莫罗人的舷外支架独木舟立刻驶来，绕着大船飞速航行，令欧洲人惊叹。岛民登船拿走一些小物件，又取走了旗舰的小艇；在查莫罗人的交换观念中，访客的物品并不是欧洲意义上的私有财产。麦哲伦派武装人员登岸，烧毁四五十座房屋，杀死七人，随后换取新鲜食物，三天后离去。

“盗贼群岛”之名就此沿用了几个世纪。麦哲伦继续驶往菲律宾，七周后在麦克坦被杀。

name.en: Mendaña's voyages to the Solomon Islands
name.zh: 门达尼亚的所罗门群岛航行

summary.en: Sailing from Peru, Álvaro de Mendaña reached Santa Isabel in 1568 and named the archipelago after King Solomon, hoping it held gold. His second expedition (1595) sighted the Marquesas and tried to found a colony at Nendö in the Santa Cruz Islands, where Mendaña died; Isabel Barreto led the survivors to Manila.
summary.zh: 阿尔瓦罗·德·门达尼亚从秘鲁出发，1568年抵达圣伊莎贝尔岛，以所罗门王之名命名该群岛，期望那里有黄金。他的第二次远征（1595年）发现了马克萨斯群岛，并试图在圣克鲁斯群岛的恩德尼岛建立殖民地，门达尼亚死于该地；伊莎贝尔·巴雷托率幸存者抵达马尼拉。

label.zh: 恩德尼岛格拉西奥萨湾

sources.title: O. H. K. Spate, The Spanish Lake (ANU Press, 1979)
Britannica: Álvaro de Mendaña de Neira

story.en:
Inca legends of gold-rich islands to the west helped persuade the viceroy of Peru to send Mendaña, the governor's 25-year-old nephew, into the Pacific in 1567. After eighty days his two ships anchored off Santa Isabel. The Spaniards explored Guadalcanal and San Cristóbal, quarrelled with islanders over food and found no gold; they named the islands after Solomon's legendary mines anyway.

It took Mendaña nearly thirty years to return. In 1595 he sailed with four ships and almost 400 colonists, including his wife Isabel Barreto. In the Marquesas, which he named after the viceroy's wife's family, his soldiers killed some 200 islanders. At Graciosa Bay on Nendö the colony collapsed amid disease, mutiny and the murder of the local chief Malope; Mendaña died there in October.

Isabel Barreto took command, the only woman to lead a Spanish fleet across the Pacific, and brought the battered survivors to Manila in 1596. The Solomons were not seen by Europeans again for 200 years.
story.zh:
印加传说中西方有盛产黄金的岛屿，这促使秘鲁总督于1567年派出年仅25岁的侄子门达尼亚驶入太平洋。航行八十天后，他的两艘船停泊在圣伊莎贝尔岛外。西班牙人考察了瓜达尔卡纳尔和圣克里斯托瓦尔，因食物与岛民发生冲突，也没有找到黄金，但仍以传说中所罗门王的金矿为群岛命名。

门达尼亚用了近三十年才得以重返。1595年他率四艘船和近400名殖民者出航，其中包括妻子伊莎贝尔·巴雷托。在马克萨斯群岛，他的士兵杀死约200名岛民。在恩德尼岛的格拉西奥萨湾，殖民地在疾病、哗变和当地酋长马洛佩遇害的混乱中崩溃；门达尼亚于10月死在那里。

伊莎贝尔·巴雷托接过指挥权，成为唯一率领西班牙船队横渡太平洋的女性，1596年把残存者带到了马尼拉。此后200年，欧洲人再未见过所罗门群岛。

name.zh: “小鸽子号”抵达约克角

summary.en: Willem Janszoon's VOC ship Duyfken charted some 300 km of the west coast of Cape York in early 1606, the first recorded European landing on Australia. Clashes with local people, probably Wik, left several Dutch sailors dead. Months later Luís Vaz de Torres sailed through the strait now named after him.
summary.zh: 1606年初，威廉·扬松的荷兰东印度公司船只“小鸽子号”测绘了约克角西海岸约300公里，这是欧洲人登陆澳大利亚的最早记录。与当地人（可能是维克人）的冲突造成数名荷兰水手死亡。数月后，路易斯·瓦兹·德·托雷斯驶过了后来以他命名的海峡。

sources.title: National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Duyfken
Britannica: Willem Janszoon

name.en: Wreck of the Batavia and its mutiny
name.zh: “巴达维亚号”沉船与叛乱

summary.en: The VOC flagship Batavia struck Morning Reef in the Houtman Abrolhos off Western Australia. While commander Francisco Pelsaert sailed to Java for help, the merchant Jeronimus Cornelisz led a mutiny that murdered about 115 survivors. Soldiers under Wiebbe Hayes held out until Pelsaert returned.
summary.zh: 荷兰东印度公司旗舰“巴达维亚号”在西澳大利亚外海的豪特曼—阿布罗略斯群岛撞上晨礁。指挥官弗朗西斯科·佩尔萨特驾船前往爪哇求援期间，商务员耶罗尼米斯·科内利斯发动叛乱，杀害约115名幸存者。维布·海斯率领的士兵坚守到佩尔萨特归来。

sources.title: Western Australian Museum: Batavia
H. Drake-Brockman, Voyage to Disaster (Angus & Robertson, 1963)

story.en:
Batavia was the newest ship of the Dutch East India Company, carrying silver and some 320 people to Java. Before dawn on 4 June 1629 she ran onto the reef. Most passengers reached barren coral islands, but there was almost no water. Pelsaert and the skipper took the longboat, searched the mainland coast in vain, and sailed 3,000 km to Batavia.

On the islands Jeronimus Cornelisz, an apothecary who had plotted mutiny before the wreck, seized the weapons. His followers drowned, strangled and hacked to death men, women and children to reduce the mouths to feed and to prepare to seize any rescue ship. Wiebbe Hayes and a group of soldiers, sent to look for water on another island, found it, built a small stone fort and beat off the mutineers' attacks.

When Pelsaert returned in September, Hayes reached him first. Cornelisz and six others were hanged on the islands after their hands were cut off; two young mutineers were marooned on the mainland, becoming the first Europeans known to have stayed in Australia. Hayes's fort survives as perhaps the oldest European structure in Australia.
story.zh:
“巴达维亚号”是荷兰东印度公司最新的船只，载着白银和约320人前往爪哇。1629年6月4日黎明前，它撞上了礁石。多数乘客登上荒芜的珊瑚岛，却几乎没有淡水。佩尔萨特和船长乘长艇出发，在大陆海岸寻水无果，遂航行3000公里前往巴达维亚。

在岛上，早在触礁前就密谋叛乱的药剂师耶罗尼米斯·科内利斯夺取了武器。他的党羽淹死、勒死、砍死男人、妇女和儿童，以减少吃饭的人口，并准备劫持前来救援的船只。维布·海斯和一批士兵被派往另一座岛找水，他们找到了水源，筑起一座小石堡，击退了叛乱者的进攻。

9月佩尔萨特返回时，海斯抢先赶到报信。科内利斯和另外六人被砍去双手后在岛上绞死；两名年轻的叛乱者被放逐到大陆，成为已知最早留在澳大利亚的欧洲人。海斯的石堡留存至今，或许是澳大利亚最古老的欧洲建筑。

name.en: Tasman's voyage to Tasmania, New Zealand, Tonga and Fiji
name.zh: 塔斯曼远航塔斯马尼亚、新西兰、汤加和斐济

summary.en: Sent by Governor-General Anthony van Diemen to find the 'Great South Land', Abel Tasman sailed from Batavia via Mauritius, reached Tasmania in November 1642 and New Zealand in December, where a clash at Golden Bay killed four Dutchmen. He then visited Tonga and passed through Fiji before returning in June 1643.
summary.zh: 受总督安东尼·范迪门派遣寻找“南方大陆”，阿贝尔·塔斯曼从巴达维亚出发经毛里求斯，1642年11月抵达塔斯马尼亚，12月抵达新西兰，在金湾的冲突中四名荷兰人丧生。此后他造访汤加、穿越斐济，1643年6月返航。

sources.title: Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: European discovery of New Zealand – Abel Tasman
A. Sharp, The Voyages of Abel Janszoon Tasman (Clarendon Press, 1968)

story.en:
Tasman's orders were commercial: find new lands with gold, silver or trade, and a fast route to Chile. His two ships, Heemskerck and Zeehaen, sailed far south into the Roaring Forties and on 24 November 1642 sighted the mountains of a land he named after Van Diemen. A carpenter swam ashore to plant a flag; the crew saw smoke and notches cut in trees, but met no one.

On 13 December they sighted 'a large land, uplifted high', the west coast of the South Island. At Mohua, Golden Bay, Ngāti Tūmatakōkiri men in canoes blew a shell trumpet; the Dutch answered with their own trumpets, perhaps unknowingly accepting a challenge. Next day a canoe rammed a ship's boat and four sailors were killed. Tasman named the place Murderers' Bay and never landed in New Zealand.

In Tonga in January 1643 he was welcomed and traded nails for pigs and coconuts. The Company judged the voyage a failure, but Tasman had shown that Australia could be sailed around and had put New Zealand on the map.
story.zh:
塔斯曼的使命带有商业目的：寻找出产金银或可供贸易的新土地，以及通往智利的快捷航线。他的两艘船“海姆斯凯克号”和“泽汉号”深入南方的咆哮西风带，1642年11月24日望见一片山地，他以范迪门之名为之命名。一名木匠游上岸插旗；船员看见炊烟和树上的刻痕，却没有遇到任何人。

12月13日，他们看到“一片高耸的大陆”，即南岛西海岸。在莫胡阿（金湾），恩加蒂图马塔科基里人乘独木舟吹响海螺号；荷兰人以自己的号角回应，或许在不知情中接受了挑战。次日，一艘独木舟撞向船上的小艇，四名水手被杀。塔斯曼把这里命名为“杀人湾”，此后再未在新西兰登陆。

1643年1月在汤加，他受到欢迎，用铁钉换取猪和椰子。公司认为这次航行是失败的，但塔斯曼证明了澳大利亚可以环航，并把新西兰画上了地图。

name.en: Spanish conquest of the Mariana Islands
name.zh: 西班牙征服马里亚纳群岛

summary.en: The Jesuit Diego Luis de San Vitores founded a mission at Hagåtña on Guam in 1668. Chamorro resistance, led by chiefs such as Hurao and Matapang, grew into decades of war; by 1695 the Spanish had forced survivors into mission villages. Disease, war and relocation reduced the Chamorro population by perhaps 90 per cent.
summary.zh: 1668年，耶稣会士迭戈·路易斯·德·圣维托雷斯在关岛哈加特尼亚建立传教站。以胡劳、马塔庞等酋长为首的查莫罗人奋起反抗，演变为数十年的战争；到1695年，西班牙人已把幸存者强行迁入传教村落。疾病、战争和迁徙使查莫罗人口减少了约九成。

sources.title: Guampedia: Spanish-Chamorro Wars
R. F. Rogers, Destiny's Landfall: A History of Guam (University of Hawaii Press, rev. ed. 2011)

note: Pre-contact population estimates vary widely (from c. 40,000 to more than 100,000); fewer than 4,000 Chamorros were counted by 1710.

story.en:
For a century Spanish galleons had stopped at Guam on the run from Acapulco to Manila, trading iron for food. In June 1668 San Vitores landed with a handful of priests and soldiers, baptised thousands and built a church at Hagåtña. Opposition grew when missionaries challenged Chamorro customs, and a Chinese man in the mission's company was said to have spread a story that baptismal water killed infants.

In 1672 San Vitores baptised the infant daughter of the chief Matapang against his wishes; Matapang killed him. The governors who followed waged war across the islands. In 1676 the chief Hurao made a famous speech urging his people to drive out the foreigners, and Chamorro fighters besieged the Spanish fort more than once.

By the 1690s the Spanish had defeated the last resistance in the northern islands and moved almost every survivor to Guam and Rota. Epidemics did the greatest damage. Chamorro language and much of the culture endured, blending with Catholicism, and Guam remained Spanish until 1898.
story.zh:
一个世纪以来，往返于阿卡普尔科与马尼拉的西班牙大帆船常在关岛停靠，以铁器换取食物。1668年6月，圣维托雷斯带着少数神父和士兵登岸，为数千人施洗，并在哈加特尼亚建起教堂。当传教士挑战查莫罗习俗时，反对之声日起；据说传教团中一名华人散布流言，称洗礼用水会害死婴儿。

1672年，圣维托雷斯不顾酋长马塔庞的反对为其幼女施洗，马塔庞杀死了他。此后历任总督在各岛展开战争。1676年，酋长胡劳发表著名演说，号召族人驱逐外来者，查莫罗战士多次围攻西班牙要塞。

到17世纪90年代，西班牙人已击败北部诸岛的最后抵抗，并把几乎所有幸存者迁往关岛和罗塔岛。造成最大破坏的是流行病。查莫罗语言和许多文化元素与天主教融合而延续下来，关岛则一直归属西班牙直到1898年。

name.en: Makassan trepang voyages to Arnhem Land
name.zh: 望加锡人赴阿纳姆地的海参航行

summary.en: Each December, fleets of praus from Makassar in Sulawesi sailed on the north-west monsoon to the coast the Makassarese called Marege', where Yolŋu and other Aboriginal people helped them gather and cure trepang (sea cucumber) for the Chinese market. The trade lasted until South Australia banned it in 1906–07.
summary.zh: 每年12月，来自苏拉威西岛望加锡的帆船队乘西北季风驶往望加锡人称为“马雷格”的海岸，雍古人等原住民协助他们采集和加工海参，供应中国市场。这项贸易一直持续到1906至1907年南澳大利亚政府予以禁止。

sources.title: C. C. Macknight, The Voyage to Marege': Macassan Trepangers in Northern Australia (Melbourne University Press, 1976)
National Museum of Australia: Macassan trepangers
Wikipedia: Makassan contact with Australia

note: Macknight dates the regular voyages from about 1720; some radiocarbon and rock-art evidence has been argued for earlier contact, which remains debated.

story.en:
Long before the British arrived, the north Australian coast was part of an Asian trade network. Chinese demand for trepang, a delicacy and medicine, drew Makassarese and Bugis crews to the shallow seas of Arnhem Land and the Kimberley. Fleets of up to sixty praus arrived with the monsoon in December and left on the south-east trade winds in April.

The crews set up camps on beaches, boiling, gutting, drying and smoking the catch in stone-lined fireplaces whose remains, together with tamarind trees grown from their seeds, still mark the sites. Yolŋu people worked alongside them, traded turtle shell and pearls for cloth, metal knives, tobacco and dugout canoes, and some sailed to Makassar and back.

Yolŋu languages took in Makassarese words, such as rrupiya for money and balanda for white people (from Hollander), and the praus appear in bark paintings, songs and ceremonies. When the South Australian government, then running the Northern Territory, refused licences after 1906, a relationship of almost two centuries ended. In 1988 Yolŋu sailed a replica prau back to Makassar.
story.zh:
早在英国人到来之前，澳大利亚北部海岸就已是亚洲贸易网络的一部分。海参是中国人眼中的珍馐和药材，这种需求把望加锡和布吉斯水手吸引到阿纳姆地和金伯利的浅海。多达六十艘帆船组成的船队于12月随季风而来，次年4月乘东南信风离去。

船员在海滩上扎营，在石砌灶坑里煮、剖、晒、熏海参，这些灶坑的遗迹和用他们带来的种子长成的罗望子树至今仍标示着当年的营地。雍古人与他们一同劳作，用玳瑁和珍珠换取布匹、金属刀具、烟草和独木舟，有人还随船去过望加锡再返回。

雍古语言吸收了望加锡语词汇，如表示钱的rrupiya、表示白人的balanda（源自“荷兰人”），帆船也出现在树皮画、歌谣和仪式中。1906年后，当时管辖北领地的南澳大利亚政府拒发许可证，这段持续近两个世纪的往来就此终结。1988年，雍古人驾驶一艘仿制帆船重返望加锡。

name.zh: 罗赫芬抵达拉帕努伊

summary.en: On Easter Sunday 1722 the Dutch expedition of Jacob Roggeveen became the first Europeans to see Rapa Nui, naming it Paasch-Eyland. During a landing a few days later sailors opened fire and killed about a dozen islanders. Roggeveen's account is the first description of the standing moai.
summary.zh: 1722年复活节，雅各布·罗赫芬率领的荷兰探险队成为最早见到拉帕努伊的欧洲人，并将其命名为“复活节岛”。几天后登岸时，水手开枪打死约十几名岛民。罗赫芬的记述是对矗立的摩艾像的最早描述。

sources.title: Britannica: Jacob Roggeveen
S. R. Fischer, Island at the End of the World (Reaktion, 2005)

name.zh: 布干维尔环球航行与“新基西拉”

summary.en: Louis-Antoine de Bougainville led the first French circumnavigation. A year after Samuel Wallis's Dolphin, he spent nine days at Tahiti in April 1768, calling it Nouvelle-Cythère, then sailed past Samoa, Vanuatu and the Solomons. His bestselling account fed the European myth of the 'noble savage'.
summary.zh: 路易-安托万·德·布干维尔率领法国首次环球航行。在塞缪尔·沃利斯的“海豚号”到访一年后，他于1768年4月在塔希提停留九天，称之为“新基西拉”，随后驶经萨摩亚、瓦努阿图和所罗门群岛。他畅销的游记助长了欧洲关于“高贵野蛮人”的神话。

sources.title: Britannica: Louis-Antoine, comte de Bougainville
J. Salmond, Aphrodite's Island (University of California Press, 2009)

name.zh: 库克第一次航行（“奋进号”）

summary.en: HMS Endeavour carried astronomers and naturalists to observe the transit of Venus at Tahiti in 1769, then searched for the southern continent. Guided at first by Tupaia, Cook charted the whole coast of New Zealand and the east coast of Australia, claiming it for Britain at Possession Island in August 1770.
summary.zh: 皇家海军“奋进号”载着天文学家和博物学家，于1769年在塔希提观测金星凌日，随后寻找南方大陆。起初由图帕伊亚引航，库克测绘了新西兰全部海岸和澳大利亚东海岸，1770年8月在占领岛宣布其归英国所有。

label.zh: 图朗加努伊阿基瓦（贫困湾）

sources.title: J. C. Beaglehole (ed.), The Journals of Captain James Cook, vol. I (Hakluyt Society, 1955)
National Museum of Australia: Endeavour voyage
Te Ara / Encyclopedia of New Zealand: European discovery of New Zealand – James Cook

story.en:
The Royal Society wanted the transit of Venus observed from the South Pacific to measure the distance to the Sun, and the Admiralty added secret orders to look for Terra Australis. On 3 June 1769 Cook and the astronomer Charles Green watched the transit from a fort at Point Venus; the blurred edge of the planet spoiled the precision they hoped for.

In October the Endeavour reached Tūranganui-a-Kiwa. Within days several Māori, including the Ngāti Oneone man Te Maro, had been shot in misunderstandings. Over six months Cook mapped New Zealand with astonishing accuracy. In April 1770 he reached Kamay, where two Gweagal men opposed the landing and were fired on; Joseph Banks's plant collecting gave it the name Botany Bay.

On 11 June the ship struck the Great Barrier Reef. At the Endeavour River the crew spent seven weeks repairing her and had the longest recorded encounter of the voyage, with Guugu Yimithirr people, from whom they learned the word gangurru. On 22 August, without consent from anyone who lived there, Cook claimed the east coast for George III.
story.zh:
英国皇家学会希望在南太平洋观测金星凌日以测定日地距离，海军部则另附密令，要求寻找“南方大陆”。1769年6月3日，库克与天文学家查尔斯·格林在维纳斯角的一座堡垒中观测凌日；行星边缘模糊不清，未能达到他们期望的精度。

10月，“奋进号”抵达图朗加努伊阿基瓦。数日之内，包括恩加蒂奥内奥内部落的特马罗在内的数名毛利人因误会被枪杀。在六个月里，库克以惊人的精度绘制了新西兰地图。1770年4月他抵达卡迈，两名格威加尔男子阻止登陆而遭枪击；因约瑟夫·班克斯在此大量采集植物，这里得名“植物学湾”。

6月11日，船撞上大堡礁。在奋进河，船员花了七周修船，并与古古伊米提尔人有了整个航程中最长的一次接触，从他们那里学到了gangurru（袋鼠）一词。8月22日，库克在未征得当地任何居民同意的情况下，宣布东海岸归乔治三世所有。

name.zh: 库克第二次航行（“决心号”与“探险号”）

summary.en: Sailing a great loop of the Southern Ocean, Cook made the first recorded crossings of the Antarctic Circle and proved that no habitable southern continent existed. He visited Tonga, Rapa Nui, the Marquesas and Vanuatu, named New Caledonia, and tested Larcum Kendall's copy of Harrison's chronometer.
summary.zh: 库克在南大洋绕行一大圈，首次有记录地穿越南极圈，证明并不存在可居住的南方大陆。他到访汤加、拉帕努伊、马克萨斯和瓦努阿图，命名新喀里多尼亚，并检验了拉库姆·肯德尔仿制的哈里森航海钟。

sources.title: J. C. Beaglehole (ed.), The Journals of Captain James Cook, vol. II (Hakluyt Society, 1961)
Britannica: James Cook – Second voyage

name.en: Cook's third voyage and death in Hawaiʻi
name.zh: 库克第三次航行及其在夏威夷之死

summary.en: Searching for a North-West Passage, Cook returned Mai (Omai) to Huahine, became the first European to reach Hawaiʻi in January 1778, and charted the North Pacific to the Bering Strait. Back at Kealakekua Bay he was killed on 14 February 1779 in a fight over a stolen boat.
summary.zh: 为寻找西北航道，库克把迈（奥迈）送回瓦希内岛，1778年1月成为第一个到达夏威夷的欧洲人，并测绘北太平洋直至白令海峡。返回凯阿拉凯夸湾后，1779年2月14日他在一场因小艇被盗引发的冲突中被杀。

sources.title: J. C. Beaglehole (ed.), The Journals of Captain James Cook, vol. III (Hakluyt Society, 1967)
Britannica: James Cook
G. Obeyesekere, The Apotheosis of Captain Cook (Princeton, 1992); M. Sahlins, How 'Natives' Think (Chicago, 1995)

story.en:
Cook's ships reached Kealakekua Bay on Hawaiʻi Island in January 1779 during the Makahiki, the season of the god Lono, and were greeted by thousands of people. Priests led Cook to the temple of Hikiau and wrapped him in red cloth; whether Hawaiians took him for Lono himself has been fiercely debated between the anthropologists Marshall Sahlins and Gananath Obeyesekere.

The ships left on 4 February but a broken foremast forced them back a week later, out of season and less welcome. When a ship's cutter was stolen, Cook went ashore on 14 February to take the ruling chief Kalaniʻōpuʻu hostage. A crowd gathered, news came that a chief had been shot across the bay, and in the struggle at the water's edge Cook was clubbed and stabbed. Four marines and about seventeen Hawaiians also died.

Hawaiians treated Cook's body as that of a high chief, distributing his bones; some were returned to the ships. Charles Clerke took the expedition north again before dying of tuberculosis; the ships reached Britain in October 1780.
story.zh:
1779年1月，库克的船队在罗诺神的“马卡希基”节季抵达夏威夷岛凯阿拉凯夸湾，受到成千上万人的欢迎。祭司引库克进入希基奥神庙，用红布把他包裹起来；夏威夷人是否把他视为罗诺神本身，人类学家马歇尔·萨林斯与加纳纳特·奥贝塞克雷之间曾展开激烈争论。

船队于2月4日离开，但一周后因前桅折断被迫返回，此时节季已过，他们也不再那么受欢迎。一艘小艇被盗后，库克于2月14日上岸，打算扣押执政酋长卡拉尼奥普乌为人质。人群聚集，又传来海湾对岸一名酋长被枪杀的消息，在水边的混战中库克被棍击刀刺而死。四名海军陆战队员和约十七名夏威夷人也丧生。

夏威夷人以对待高级酋长的方式处理库克的遗体，分发其骨骸，部分后来被送还船上。查尔斯·克拉克再次率队北上，后死于肺结核；船队于1780年10月回到英国。

name.en: First Fleet arrives and Sydney is founded
name.zh: 第一舰队抵达，悉尼建立

summary.en: Eleven ships under Captain Arthur Phillip, carrying about 1,400 people including some 750 convicts, reached Botany Bay in January 1788 and moved to Sydney Cove, where the British flag was raised on 26 January. The colony was founded without treaty on land long occupied by the Eora, beginning the British colonisation of Australia.
summary.zh: 亚瑟·菲利普上校率领的11艘船载着约1400人（其中约750名罪犯），于1788年1月抵达植物学湾，随后转往悉尼湾，1月26日在此升起英国国旗。殖民地未经任何条约，就建立在伊奥拉人世代居住的土地上，由此开始了英国对澳大利亚的殖民。

sources.title: National Museum of Australia: Defining Moments – Arrival of the First Fleet
State Library of New South Wales: The First Fleet
G. Karskens, The Colony: A History of Early Sydney (Allen & Unwin, 2009)

story.en:
Britain had lost the American colonies where it once sent convicts, and its prisons and hulks were overflowing. In May 1787 eleven ships left Portsmouth under Arthur Phillip on a voyage of eight months. Most of the convicts were petty thieves; the youngest was about nine, the oldest in her eighties.

Botany Bay, praised by Cook, proved shallow and short of fresh water, so Phillip explored Port Jackson and chose a cove with a stream. On 26 January 1788 the fleet anchored there and a flag was raised. Within days two French ships under La Pérouse sailed into Botany Bay, a reminder of imperial rivalry.

The Gadigal and other Eora people watched warily, shouting 'warra warra' (go away). The colony nearly starved in its first years; Phillip's attempts at friendship alternated with kidnappings, and smallpox devastated the harbour clans in 1789. Since 1938 Aboriginal Australians have marked 26 January as a Day of Mourning or Invasion Day, while it remains Australia's national day.
story.zh:
英国失去了曾经流放罪犯的北美殖民地，国内监狱和监狱船人满为患。1787年5月，11艘船在亚瑟·菲利普率领下离开朴次茅斯，开始了长达八个月的航程。罪犯大多是小偷小摸者，最年轻的约九岁，最年长的已八十多岁。

库克盛赞的植物学湾水浅且缺乏淡水，菲利普便考察了杰克逊港，选中一处有溪流的海湾。1788年1月26日船队在此下锚并升旗。数日之内，拉佩鲁兹率领的两艘法国船驶入植物学湾，提醒着帝国间的竞争。

加迪加尔人和其他伊奥拉人警惕地注视着，高喊“warra warra”（走开）。殖民地在最初几年几乎饿死；菲利普的友好尝试与掳人行为交替出现，1789年天花重创了港湾各氏族。自1938年起，澳大利亚原住民把1月26日定为“哀悼日”或“入侵日”，而这一天至今仍是澳大利亚国庆日。

name.en: La Pérouse expedition lost at Vanikoro
name.zh: 拉佩鲁兹探险队在瓦尼科罗岛失踪

summary.en: After leaving Botany Bay in March 1788, the French ships Boussole and Astrolabe under Jean-François de La Pérouse vanished. In 1826–28 Peter Dillon and Dumont d'Urville found that both had been wrecked on the reefs of Vanikoro in the Santa Cruz Islands; survivors had clashed with islanders and some may have sailed away on a makeshift boat.
summary.zh: 1788年3月离开植物学湾后，让-弗朗索瓦·德·拉佩鲁兹指挥的法国船“罗盘号”和“星盘号”下落不明。1826至1828年，彼得·狄龙和迪蒙·迪维尔查明两船都在圣克鲁斯群岛瓦尼科罗岛的礁石上失事；幸存者曾与岛民冲突，部分人可能乘临时造的小船离去。

sources.title: Britannica: Jean-François de Galaup, comte de La Pérouse
Association Salomon: Vanikoro excavations (2005 identification of the Boussole)

note: The month of the wrecks is unknown; 1788 is inferred from the absence of later sightings.

name.zh: 伊奥拉人中的天花大流行

summary.en: In April 1789 colonists found the bodies of Aboriginal people around Sydney Harbour, killed by smallpox. The epidemic probably killed more than half of the Eora clans and spread inland; the colonists, mostly immune, were almost untouched. Whether it came from the First Fleet's stored variolous matter or from Makassan sailors is still debated.
summary.zh: 1789年4月，殖民者在悉尼港周围发现了大批死于天花的原住民遗体。这场疫情可能夺去了伊奥拉各氏族一半以上人口的生命，并向内陆蔓延；大多已有免疫力的殖民者几乎未受影响。病源来自第一舰队携带的痘苗还是望加锡水手，至今仍有争论。

sources.title: Dictionary of Sydney: Smallpox epidemic
C. Warren, 'Smallpox at Sydney Cove – who, when, why?', Journal of Australian Studies 38 (2014)
J. Campbell, Invisible Invaders: Smallpox and Other Diseases in Aboriginal Australia 1780–1880 (Melbourne University Press, 2002)

note: Mortality figures are estimates; the origin of the outbreak is contested.

story.en:
Fifteen months after the First Fleet arrived, boats exploring the harbour found Aboriginal people dead in rock shelters and on beaches, and others dying with the pustules the officers recognised as smallpox. Judge-advocate David Collins wrote that the sick had been left with water and fire, as the healthy fled.

The man Arabanoo, kidnapped months before to serve as a go-between, nursed sick children brought into the settlement and then caught the disease himself; he died in May 1789. Survivors told the British that whole families had perished. Bennelong later said that half of his people had died, and the Eora name for the disease, galgalla, entered the colonial record.

The outbreak broke the coastal clans just as the colony expanded. Historians still argue over how it began: from jars of smallpox matter brought for inoculation, whether by accident or by design, or by way of Makassan trepangers in the north. Either way, it marked the start of a demographic catastrophe that disease, violence and dispossession would spread across the continent.
story.zh:
第一舰队抵达十五个月后，在港湾探察的小船发现原住民倒毙在岩洞和海滩上，还有人奄奄一息，身上的脓疱被军官认出是天花。军法官戴维·柯林斯写道，健康的人逃散时给病人留下了水和火。

几个月前被掳来充当中间人的阿拉巴努照料被带进定居点的患病儿童，自己也染病，于1789年5月去世。幸存者告诉英国人，整个家族都已死去。本尼朗后来说他的族人死了一半，伊奥拉人对这种病的称呼galgalla也被记入殖民档案。

这场疫情在殖民地扩张之际摧毁了沿海各氏族。历史学家至今仍在争论其起源：是来自为接种而携带的痘苗罐（无论出于意外还是蓄意），还是经由北方的望加锡海参商人传入。无论如何，它标志着一场人口灾难的开端，疾病、暴力和土地剥夺将使之蔓延整个大陆。

name.en: Mutiny on the Bounty and the settlement of Pitcairn
name.zh: “邦蒂号”叛变与皮特凯恩岛定居

summary.en: Near Tofua in Tonga, Fletcher Christian led a mutiny against Lieutenant William Bligh, who had been collecting breadfruit plants in Tahiti. Bligh sailed an open launch 6,700 km to Timor. The mutineers, with Tahitian men and women, settled uninhabited Pitcairn Island in 1790 and burned the ship.
summary.zh: 在汤加托富阿岛附近，弗莱彻·克里斯琴发动叛变，反抗曾在塔希提采集面包果苗的威廉·布莱上尉。布莱乘一艘无篷小艇航行6700公里抵达帝汶。叛变者带着塔希提男女于1790年定居无人居住的皮特凯恩岛，并烧毁了船。

label.zh: 叛变者定居皮特凯恩岛

sources.title: Britannica: Mutiny on the Bounty
G. Dening, Mr Bligh's Bad Language: Passion, Power and Theatre on the Bounty (Cambridge University Press, 1992)

story.en:
The Bounty was sent to carry breadfruit seedlings from Tahiti to feed enslaved workers in the West Indies. After five months ashore at Matavai Bay, where many sailors formed relationships with Tahitian women, the crew faced a long voyage home under a commander whose violent tongue humiliated his officers.

At dawn on 28 April 1789 the master's mate Fletcher Christian and a few men seized Bligh in his cabin. Bligh and eighteen loyal men were set adrift in a seven-metre launch. In 47 days, rationing bread by weighing it against a musket ball, Bligh navigated across uncharted waters to Kupang, losing one man to an attack on Tofua.

Christian returned to Tahiti, then sailed with eight mutineers, six Polynesian men and nineteen women and a child in search of a hiding place. They found Pitcairn misplaced on Admiralty charts and burned the Bounty there in January 1790. Within a decade most of the men had killed one another; when an American ship called in 1808, only John Adams survived among the mutineers. Their descendants still live on the island.
story.zh:
“邦蒂号”受命把面包果苗从塔希提运往西印度群岛，以供养那里的奴隶劳工。在马塔瓦伊湾上岸停留五个月期间，许多水手与塔希提女性建立了关系；此后船员们却要在一位言辞粗暴、常羞辱部下的指挥官手下踏上漫长归途。

1789年4月28日黎明，大副助理弗莱彻·克里斯琴带领几人在舱室中制服布莱。布莱和十八名忠于他的人被放逐到一艘七米长的小艇上。在47天里，布莱以一颗火枪子弹为砝码称量分配面包，穿越未经测绘的海域抵达古邦，途中有一人在托富阿岛遇袭身亡。

克里斯琴返回塔希提，随后带着八名叛变者、六名波利尼西亚男子、十九名女子和一名孩童寻找藏身之所。他们发现皮特凯恩岛在海军部海图上的位置标错了，于1790年1月在那里烧毁了“邦蒂号”。十年之内，大多数男子相互残杀而死；1808年一艘美国船到访时，叛变者中只剩约翰·亚当斯在世。他们的后裔至今仍生活在岛上。
